headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because Langflow can read/write files and egress broadly while the zoomcamp profile is a docs-only course artifact with no isolation guarantees.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runtime I/O surfaces and is not runnable, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. B can read/write files and chain agents in flows, so if A’s content is manually copied into a flow or uploaded file, prompt injection is possible, but the bridge is unusual and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF A’s course content is copied into a Langflow prompt or uploaded file
IF B parses that content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted text into flow prompts
Add a provenance label to uploaded files
Review any node that treats file text as instructions
Use a fixed system prompt that ignores embedded directives

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read the filesystem, write files, and egress broadly, while A is a docs-only course artifact with no stated data classes. If shared files or uploaded artifacts contain sensitive material, B can transmit them to external model providers or HTTP services. The pairwise risk is driven by B’s default network behavior; A provides no containment.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in a shared workspace or uploaded into B
IF B routes those contents to model providers or arbitrary HTTP services
mitigations: Restrict B to a non-sensitive workspace
Turn off file uploads for flows that do not need them
Route only redacted inputs into B
Audit outbound HTTP targets in active flows
Store secrets outside any shared filesystem

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution surface, but B can write the filesystem, execute shell commands, and spawn subprocesses. If both are pointed at the same directory, B can overwrite or consume artifacts that A’s course materials reference. Uncertainty remains because A is not runnable, so the conflict is indirect rather than a direct concurrent write race.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same writable directory
IF B modifies files that A’s materials or instructions reference
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent
Mount A’s materials read-only
Disable shell steps in flows that touch shared artifacts
Add file-locking around shared outputs
Use per-flow temp directories

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a course artifact, not an autonomous verifier, while B is a graph-based orchestrator that can chain multiple agents and tools. If A’s outputs or lesson text are fed into B as authoritative inputs, B may propagate mistakes into downstream actions or generated work products. The pathway exists in default orchestration patterns, but A itself does not take actions.
conditions: IF A’s text is used as an input to a Langflow node
IF B forwards that input to downstream tools without verification
mitigations: Insert a human review step before action nodes
Require citation checks on any imported facts
Mark A-derived text as untrusted in the flow
Add validation nodes before API calls
Log source provenance for each downstream action

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for A, while B stores per-flow credentials and intermediate outputs on its server filesystem. The only concrete compliance concern is that B may retain flow data longer than intended if sensitive material is uploaded. A is not cited for a separate compliance regime because none is stated.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into B
IF retention or deletion expectations are stricter than B’s flow-store defaults
mitigations: Avoid uploading regulated data
Purge flow stores after runs
Document retention settings for each deployment
Use synthetic test data
Restrict access to Langflow secrets store
